newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy centre-right confirms will fight budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy centre-right confirms will fight budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance on Friday confirmed it would put up a stiff fight against Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cost-cutting 1997 budget.

"There should be no confusion between the role of the majority and the role of the opposition which must and will remain absolutely distinct," former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi said in a statement.
Berlusconi spoke after opposition party leaders held a meeting to discuss their opposition to the budget.
"We will discuss the budget in parliament by offering a stiff opposition," said PierFerdinando Casini, leader of a small party in the centre-right alliance.
The meeting was held after a letter the alliance sent to President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro had been interpreted as a possibile softening of the opposition's stand on the budget.
Berlusconi said the letter to Scalfaro warned that Prodi should not resort to what it called "exaggerated and incorrect use" of confidence votes to get the budget throught parliament.
Prodi has said he will use confidence votes if necessary.
The 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) budget aims at trying to help Italy make the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
Opposition parties say its emphasis on revenue raising will unfairly hurt the middle class, merchants and shopkeepers.
Prodi depends on external support in the lower house from the hard left party Communist Refoundation for his government's majority.
He received comfort on Friday when Fausto Bertinotti, leader of Communist Refoundation party, confirmed that the party would support the government over the budget.

The budget is due to be presented to the full chamber next Wednesday. It is due for final approval in the lower house by November 14. It then moves to the Senate and must be passed by the end of the year. -- Rome newsroom +39 6 6782505
